lessons.title: मैं पढ़ रहा था (maiṁ paṛh rahā thā) — what was going on
lessons.gloss: I was reading — the past of an action going on, and a scene with an event inside it

segments.text: Say "I am doing" and "he was". (maiṁ kar rahā hūṁ, vah thā.) Then "she came". (vah āī.) The first two make this lesson; the third will interrupt it.
मैं किताब पढ़ रहा था। maiṁ kitāb paṛh rahā thā. — "I was reading a book."
You know कर रहा हूँ, "I am doing". Put था where हूँ stood and the same action moves into the past. Both रहा and था follow the one doing it:
मैं पढ़ रहा था (maiṁ paṛh rahā thā) — I was reading; a woman says मैं पढ़ रही थी (maiṁ paṛh rahī thī).
वह सो रहा था (vah so rahā thā) — he was sleeping; वह सो रही थी (vah so rahī thī) — she was sleeping.
बारिश हो रही थी (bāriś ho rahī thī) — it was raining.
There is no ने here, even with a thing: मैं खाना खा रहा था, never मैंने. ने belongs to the plain past alone.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: a scene and an event

segments.text: जब मैं खाना खा रहा था, तब मीरा आई। jab maiṁ khānā khā rahā thā, tab Mīrā āī. — "When I was eating, Mira came."

A story needs two kinds of past. खा रहा था is the scene: it was going on, and the sentence does not say when it began or ended. आई is the event: it happened, once, inside the scene. जब … तब …, the frame you know for "when … then …", holds the two together.
जब बारिश हो रही थी, तब बिजली गई। (jab bāriś ho rahī thī, tab bijlī gaī.) — While it was raining, the power went.

segments.prompt: Say that you were reading a book when Arun came.
acceptedResponses: jab maiṁ kitāb paṛh rahā thā, tab aruṇ āyā
जब मैं किताब पढ़ रहा था, तब अरुण आया।
जब मैं किताब पढ़ रही थी, तब अरुण आया।
jab maiṁ kitāb paṛh rahī thī, tab aruṇ āyā

feedback.correct: paṛh rahā thā is the scene; āyā is the event inside it.
feedback.incorrect: The scene takes rahā thā (or rahī thī); the event is the plain past: Aruṇ āyā.

segments.text: "I was reading"? (मैं पढ़ रहा था (maiṁ paṛh rahā thā), or पढ़ रही थी.) "It was raining"? (बारिश हो रही थी.) In जब मैं खाना खा रहा था, तब मीरा आई, which is the scene and which is the event? (खा रहा था is the scene; आई is the event.) Why no ने in मैं खाना खा रहा था? (ने belongs to the plain past alone.)
Before the new one: say "I was reading a book". (maiṁ kitāb paṛh rahā thā.) Then the words for a week and a year. (haftā, sāl.)
पिछला — pichlā — "last, previous": the one before this one.
पिछले हफ़्ते मैं गाँव गया। pichle hafte maiṁ gā̃v gayā. — "Last week I went to the village."
पिछला is an adjective, and it agrees: पिछला हफ़्ता (pichlā haftā), "last week", but पिछली बार (pichlī bār), "last time", because बार is feminine.
Said as a time, "last week" or "last year" takes the form you met in बच्चे को: पिछले हफ़्ते, पिछले साल.
पिछले साल हम बहुत व्यस्त थे। pichle sāl ham bahut vyast the. — "Last year we were very busy."

पिछला (pichlā) has no row of its own in CDIAL. It is usually connected with पीछे (pīche), "behind", which CDIAL traces to paśca, "hinder part" (CDIAL 7990). The last week, on that picture, is the one behind you.

segments.instruction: "Last week I went to the village" — pichle hafte maiṁ gā̃v gayā
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "Last week I went to the village" — *pichle hafte maiṁ gā̃v gayā*]

segments.instruction: "Last time it was raining" — pichlī bār bāriś ho rahī thī
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "Last time it was raining" — *pichlī bār bāriś ho rahī thī*]

segments.text: What does पिछला (pichlā) mean? ("Last, previous".) "Last year"? (पिछले साल.) "Last time"? (पिछली बार: बार is feminine.)

segments.text: Which past is the scene? (रहा था: बारिश हो रही थी.) Which is the event? (The plain past: मीरा आई.) "Last year she read many books"? (पिछले साल उसने बहुत किताबें पढ़ीं: ने, and पढ़ीं for the books.)
